items.summary: Trump accused Yemen's Houthi militants of deliberately trying to drive up oil prices ahead of the Nov 3 US midterms, warning 'I'll be there after the elections, and I will never forget!' their attacks on Saudi Arabia. He told reporters he 'might' ask Turkish President Erdogan to intervene in support of Saudi interests ('President Erdogan, I think, would do as I ask'). Erdogan separately called Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Tuesday to condemn the Houthi attacks and pledge Turkey will stand by Saudi Arabia, as Ankara's Saudi-Pakistan defense pact heads to parliament.
items.title: Trump warns Houthis he'll 'never forget' Saudi attacks, floats Erdogan intervention

items.summary: Brent rose toward $107 a barrel on Wednesday (+0.8% to ~$106.5, WTI ~$95) after two more vessels were struck in Hormuz and Iran confirmed new anti-ship tactics aimed at keeping prices high into the midterms. Morgan Stanley raised its Dated Brent forecast by $5/bbl for this quarter and next, saying 'uncertainty around crude exports remains elevated' with Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure compounding the Hormuz disruption.
items.title: Brent toward $107 as Morgan Stanley raises Dated Brent forecast $5 on Hormuz/Houthi supply risk
